title: Square a phone on a mini tripod ball head: hold it, press the head's button, set it straight, let the button relock
instruction: Make the phone on the mini tripod level, and leave it standing level on its own.
context: People stand their phones on tabletop mini tripods for video calls, cooking recipes and filming; a crooked phone spoils every frame. On the Manfrotto PIXI mini tripod, a spring locks the ball head and frees it only while the button on the side of the head is pressed. Because the phone sits high above the ball, pressing the button without holding the phone lets the phone flop to the head's 35 degree stop. One hand holds the phone while the other pinches the button against the head, brings the phone level in both roll and tilt while the button stays pressed, and lets the button go so the head relocks. On a real bench the result is read with a phone level app on the phone's top edge and face (both within 3 degrees of level) while the trial video confirms the tripod stayed on its marks.
setup: Station bench; coordinates in m from the midpoint between the arm bases (left y = +0.305, right y = -0.305), x away from the arms, z up from the bench. Both arms start at the ready pose, grippers open. One fixed layout (object_jitter = 0); nothing varies by seed. A Manfrotto PIXI mini tripod MTPIXI-B (maker: 13.5 cm tall, 0.19 kg; about 180 mm across its feet) carrying the Manfrotto PIXI smartphone clamp MCPIXI (maker: 0.041 kg, opens 6-10.4 cm), bought separately, stands open at (0.26, 0.00) +/- 0.005 m on three yellow 24 mm tape marks at (0.350, 0.000), (0.215, +0.078) and (0.215, -0.078) m, its red push-button facing 85 degrees right of -x (towards the right arm and slightly forward). An Apple iPhone 15 (147.6 x 71.6 x 7.8 mm, 171 g; any phone of its size and mass with a level app works) sits landscape in the clamp facing the arms (-x), locked at +10.0 degrees forward/back screen tilt and -20.0 degrees top-edge roll (+/- 0.5 deg). Reset check: three feet on their tape marks, phone level app reading (+10, -20) +/- 0.5 deg, top-camera photo.
scoring: Read at the end of the trial; the trial ends early once full score has held 2 s after the 1 s rest window. Whole-trial zero rules (checked from the trial video; final photo confirms end state): score is 0 if at any moment a tripod foot lifts more than 10 mm off the bench, a tripod foot slides more than 20 mm horizontally from its start tape mark, the phone touches the bench, or the phone turns on the head while nobody presses the button, seen on the trial video (the simulator counts more than 0.2 deg). Otherwise, when both grippers are at least 30 mm from the phone, clamp, tripod and button, the button is out (within 0.5 mm of its outer stop, head locked; on the bench nothing touches the button), and all parts have been at rest (<= 0.02 m/s and <= 0.05 rad/s; on the bench nothing moves on the video) for 1.0 s: 1.0 if both phone tilt and phone roll are within 3.0 degrees of level (phone level app on face and top edge); 0.5 if both are within 8.0 degrees of level and at least one exceeds 3.0 degrees; 0.0 if either exceeds 8.0 degrees or the end conditions are not met.
reset_notes: Stand the three tripod feet on their yellow tape squares; hold the phone, press the button, set the phone to +10.0 degrees tilt and -20.0 degrees roll with a phone level app, release the button so the head locks, and check the top-camera frame; about 20 s. Nothing is consumed, sharp, hot or wet.
fidelity: Pure serial rigid-body tree on the free-standing tripod: two ball-head hinges (tilt and roll, +/- 35 deg stops) with bilateral PhysX capped-spring drives (1.50 N m locked; 0.02 N m while the 6000 N/m button slide is pressed >= 2.4 mm of its 3.0 mm, 18 N stroke). Phone welded to clamp. Sizes and masses from the makers' pages; head torques and button force are estimates, each with its derivation in README. Not modelled: rubber foot squish, clamp jaw spring and pan rotation.
